speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are here to evaluate the cause of systemic hypertension in a pediatric patient. To begin, how old is the child, and have they experienced any headaches, vision changes, or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Since he is asymptomatic at a well-child visit, are there any specific findings on the physical exam, such as an abnormal pulse, bruits, or a discrepancy in blood pressure between his arms and legs? Additionally, could you please confirm his current height and weight percentiles?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual report; migraines do not cause high blood pressure specifically in the right arm. This discrepancy suggests a possible coarctation of the aorta or subclavian stenosis. Please confirm: does he have any cold feet, weak femoral pulses, or a blood pressure difference between his arms and legs? REQUEST TEST: Blood pressure measurement in both upper extremities and both lower extremities (ankle-brachial index). REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood_Pressure_Right_Upper_Extremity: 150/80 mm Hg; Pulses: 2+ radial pulses and trace femoral pulses; Echocardiogram Findings: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal; Blood_Pressure_Differential: Upper Extremities 150/80 mm Hg (Right), Compared to lower values in lower extremities; Chest_X-ray Findings: Normal heart size, rib notching not observed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood pressure differential and trace femoral pulses confirm coarctation of the aorta, but the absence of rib notching on the chest X-ray is notable for a 5-year-old. Do you have any history of a heart murmur, or were there any prior episodes of poor weight gain or failure to thrive? REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide the full series of the Chest X-ray to ensure no subtle rib notching is missed.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.

The clinical presentation of severe hypertension in the right upper extremity combined with trace femoral pulses and echocardiographic evidence of aortic narrowing confirms this diagnosis. Given his asymptomatic status and normal LV function, please ensure the patient is referred for cardiac surgery consultation for repair.
